workouts.description: Welcome to Day 1 of Double Under Pro! Today is all about setting a baseline and deciding your best starting point. Based on how things go, you’ll either jump right into Double Under Pro or begin with Double Under Foundations, a 3-week mini-course designed to hone your double under technique. If you find counting jump rope reps difficult, video your sets and count them afterwards when reviewing the video. Download the Double Under Score Sheet found under the file icon or use the Double Under Automated Tracking Sheet.

While this course is optimized for the Heavy and Medium rope use, you can use any jump rope or combination of jump ropes you have access to. If you only have one rope, no problem! Just stick with it and complete all drills using what you’ve got.

workouts.title: DU PRO 2.2 (Week 2, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Your shoulders, elbows, and hands all play a major role in proper double under positioning. Today, we’re reinforcing the “elbows back” and “quick draw” position with some targeted banded drills. To set it up, loop a resistance band around one elbow, then pull it behind your back and around the other elbow. This will help keep your hands by your hips and mimic the ideal quick-draw position. If you tend to jump with your hands too far forward, try wrapping the band around the front of your body instead to cue proper hand placement. At the end of the session, review your video from Drill 3. Did the banded drill improve your positioning and control in your double unders?

Note that the banded arms drill we practice in Lesson 2.2 makes a comeback here. Video your last set of MAX Double Unders for post session review and see if Jedi eye closed training helped improve your DU form. 2-4 minutes Row, Bike, Slow Jog or No Jump Burpees 10 x Ankle Roll Outs + 10ft x Toe Walks + 10ft x Heel Walks 10 x Shoulder Pass-through + Overhead Squat (use PVC or jump rope) 30 sec x Child Pose 2 Sets • HEAVY 20sec x Side Swing Flow 10 sec Rest Draw a circle on the ground, about a foot in diameter with the goal of keeping all your bounds inside the circle. workouts.title: DU PRO 4.2 (Week 4, Workout 2)
workouts.description: The DU Stop Drill is money! It’s one of the best drills to build Double Under capacity with solid form. Start with 1 Double Under, then stop. If it’s a clean rep, go for 2 next time. If not, stay at that rep until you can hit it consistently. The key is not to rush it. Take your time. The goal isn’t how many reps you can string together, it’s how well you can connect big, slow single unders to double unders with as little change as possible.

workouts.title: DU PRO 5.1 (Week 5, Workout 1)
workouts.description: We’ve been working on elbow positioning and wrist snap to keep the rope moving in a smooth, circular path. When your hands drift too far forward or back, that circle breaks — and double unders become much harder to maintain. To reinforce proper alignment, draw two lines on the floor about 12 inches apart. Bound on one line and aim to have your rope strike the other. This helps train consistency in both hand placement and rope path. Today also introduces percentage programming. Use your best unbroken set from the 60 sec double under retest in Lesson 4.3 to calculate your target rep count. If you’re using the Double Under Pro Automated Tracking Sheet, it will calculate the rep percentages for you automatically.

workouts.title: DU PRO 5.2 (Week 5, Workout 2)
workouts.description: So excited for this training session! For the next four weeks, we’ll be building double under capacity using percentage-based work sets as the speed rope finally makes its debut. Your goal with the percentages is to hit each set unbroken. No need to exceed the prescribed numbers — once you hit 40%, stop there. If you can’t complete a set unbroken, that’s totally fine. Just make a note of it; we’ve got a special buyout waiting for you at the end of the session. You’ll also see the first appearance of the Ta-Ta-Tum Drill. In this drill, perform 1–2 reps while saying “Ta-Ta-Tum” out loud, in sync with the rope. “Ta” represents the rope hitting the floor, and “Tum” is the reload of your double under bound. This will help you better feel and understand the rhythm and timing of the rope.
